one_sentence: The delayed-choice quantum eraser and the Cross are the same mathematical event at different scales, with retrocausality mapping to atonement.
executive_summary: This document argues that the delayed-choice quantum eraser (Scully & Druhl 1982, Kim et al. 1999) and the Christian doctrine of the Cross are structurally isomorphic. The core claim is that a future measurement choice retroactively determines past behavior in the quantum eraser, mirroring how the Cross is an eternal event (Revelation 13:8) that projects into time. The mapping is forced, non-arbitrary, and bidirectional: physics predicts theology (retrocausality implies pre-temporal atonement) and theology predicts physics (eternal sacrifice implies retrocausal correlations). Four historical atonement theories (Penal Substitution, Christus Victor, Moral Influence, Recapitulation) are shown as projections of this single retrocausal event. The isomorphism passes all four separator tests and is classified as Level 3 (Structural Isomorphism) with high confidence, supported by experimental replication and scripture. The conclusion is that the quantum eraser experimentally demonstrates the Spirit's temporal freedom.
short_summary: This document is a structural isomorphism mapping the delayed-choice quantum eraser to the Christian doctrine of atonement. The core claim is that a future measurement choice retroactively determines past behavior in physics, mirroring how the Cross is an eternal event that projects into time. Key evidence includes the Kim et al. 1999 experiment and scriptures Revelation 13:8, Ephesians 1:4, and 1 Peter 1:20. This matters because it provides a rigorous, testable framework linking quantum mechanics and theology, with falsification criteria that allow empirical disconfirmation.
